chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Bishr al-Hudhali from Ajlan, Abu Salih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When a newborn is born, we give him wine to drink.' He said: 'Whoever gives a newborn something intoxicating, Allah will give him al-Hamim (hot water/goo), even if He forgives him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of giving wine to a newborn baby according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that administering wine to a newborn incurs the specific punishment of drinking *al-Hamim* (boiling water or pus) in Hell, a consequence that persists even if the individual is ultimately forgiven. This highlights the unique severity of introducing intoxicants to the innocent, linking the physical act to a distinct eschatological penalty. The ruling underscores the principle that actions affecting the soul's purity, even in infancy, carry weighty divine retribution.
